title: Tape Measure
hook: Pull out three metres and you wind a spring 20 turns tighter; let go and it winds the blade back in.
summary: A tape measure has to fit three metres of ruler in a pocket and bring it back by itself. It does both with steel: a blade curved across its width, stiff enough to stand out in the air yet flat enough to coil, and a spring that keeps the pull you put into it.

Your pull on the hook draws the blade off a drum, and the drum carries the outer end of a flat spiral spring round a post fixed in the case. A shoe under the front button can pinch the blade to hold it, and the hook on its end slides on its rivets.

Pull all 3 m out and the drum turns 20.3 times, moving the spring's coils off the drum's wall and onto the post; let go and the spring turns it back. Here the blade, drum and spring move together from one set of sums, and the hook slides by its own 0.9 mm as it is pulled.

parts.label: End hook
parts.about: Where your pull goes in: 0.9 mm of steel riveted to the blade's end. It slides on its rivets by exactly its own thickness, so the zero is right whether it's hooked or pushed.

parts.label: Rivets
parts.about: Two rivets fixed in the blade, running in slots in the hook 0.9 mm longer than they are.

parts.label: Blade
parts.about: 3 m of steel 0.13 mm thick and 19 mm wide, curved across its width. On the drum it lies flat, about 20 turns deep; out in the air the curve stiffens it.

parts.label: Drum
parts.about: A 44 mm hub with the blade's tail fixed to it. About 15 cm of blade turns it once; inside is the spring's barrel.

parts.label: Recoil spring
parts.about: 3.8 m of spring steel 0.13 mm thick and 16 mm wide, coiled 37 turns deep in the drum: its inner end on the post, its outer end on the drum.

parts.label: Spring post
parts.about: Moulded into the right half of the case: the spring's inner end hooks on it and the drum turns round it. It never moves, so the drum's turning winds the spring.

parts.label: Lock button
parts.about: Press it 2 mm into its recess and the shoe under it drops onto the blade.

parts.label: Brake shoe
parts.about: An arm from the button down inside the case's front wall, ending in a shoe just over the blade behind the mouth. Locked, it pinches the blade against the guide under it.

parts.label: Case, left half
parts.about: One of two moulded halves under a rubber skin; this one carries the label.

parts.label: Case, right half
parts.about: The other half: the spring's post stands from its wall, and the guide the blade runs out on is moulded into it.

parts.label: Belt clip
parts.about: Sprung steel, screwed to the case where the spring's post is.

annotations.title: The end hook
annotations.text: Your pull starts here, on 0.9 mm of steel riveted to the end of the blade. It is loose on purpose (number 6).

annotations.title: The blade
annotations.text: Steel 0.13 mm thick and 19 mm wide, curved across its width. It leaves the drum's roll at the bottom and runs out through a guide in the mouth; on the roll it lies flat, 20 turns deep.

annotations.title: The drum
annotations.text: The blade's tail is fixed to this 44 mm hub, so every 15 cm or so you pull turns it once: 20.3 turns for the whole 3 m.

annotations.title: The recoil spring
annotations.text: 3.8 m of spring steel inside the drum, its inner end on a post fixed to the case and its outer end on the drum. Pull the blade out and the drum winds it tighter, its coils moving off the drum's wall onto the post.

annotations.title: The lock
annotations.text: Press the button 2 mm and a shoe on its arm drops onto the blade just behind the mouth, pinching it against the guide under it. The spring can no longer pull it in.

annotations.title: The loose hook is meant to be
annotations.text: It isn't worn. The rivets run in slots 0.9 mm longer than they are, so the hook slides by exactly its own thickness: out when you hook an edge, in when you push against a wall. Both readings start at the true zero.

annotations.title: The case
annotations.text: Two moulded halves under a rubber skin. The right one carries the spring's post and the guide the blade runs out on.

annotations.title: The belt clip
annotations.text: Sprung steel, held by one screw into the case where the spring's post stands.

film.caption: Pull out 16 cm of blade and the drum turns once, winding the spring inside a turn tighter.
Press the lock and a shoe pinches the blade against its guide, so it stays out.
Let the lock off and the spring unwinds, turning the drum back and reeling the blade in.

extra.label: Built for this site
extra.text: The case cut into its halves and given walls, the mouth opened; the blade, drum, spring and its post, hook with slotted rivets and brake generated from a Stanley PowerLock 3 m × 19 mm and its patents. The blade's curve, the spring's size and pull, and the lock as a press are this model's own; the wrist strap is left off.
